Pajeczno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pajęczno, Poland

Demolished. Pajęczno, founded in 1265, saw Jewish settlement from the 18th century; population grew from 112 (about 10%) in 1820 to 1,042 (11.5%) by 1939. A November 21, 1940 ghetto held about 1,000 Jews from Pajęczno and surrounding areas; its August 19, 1942 liquidation deported remaining residents to Chełmno. This cemetery, most probably established in the first half of the 19th century, was reduced to a postwar gravel pit; local residents recall human bones scattered across the grounds. Excavated matzevot were destroyed during construction of modern-day Mickiewicza Street's pavement. A 2014 initiative to commemorate the site has yet to be implemented.
